closed_findings.proof: A separate CaptureBudgetError escapes ordinary per-file handling. Each next transfer is capped by remaining cumulative allowance including tar overhead and the transport's one-byte overflow check. Successful archive bytes are counted; discarded failed output is conservatively charged cap+1. Exhaustion stops normal cp/storage/HTTP work, retaining final inventory and an INCOMPLETE partial report.

limits: This closes the one R1 resource-bound blocker; accepted transport/core/read-only helpers were not broadly re-audited.

The 25MiB file-transfer allowance now accounts for tar bytes and conservative failed-output bounds, separate from metadata/storage response bounds. Synthetic evidence is not observed native byte telemetry.
Actual capture still must pass CLI/input/exact-identity checks and preserve its exclusive one-use output marker. No automatic repeat or missing-file repair follows from acceptance.
Existing filesystem-wall-time and daemon-cancellation limits remain: subprocess budgets do not guarantee arbitrary host I/O duration or daemon cancellation.

Operator's separate authorization and parent tool permission remain required for the one capture attempt. This receipt grants no new lifecycle, startup, data-write, credential-export or cutover authority.
No actual installed files, storage lineage, SDK policies, archive availability or endpoint outcome are accepted here. Capture results require their own bounded evidence review.
